Gospel_of_Mary.scope_note: Less than half of the work survives. Absence classifications mean not attested in the checked extant text, not proof of absence from the lost portions. The preserved work strongly supports differential access to revelation and dispute over Mary's vision, but not the Yaldabaoth-style local-totality sequence.

Gospel_of_Judas.scope_note: The checked stable structure distinguishes the disciples' god and cosmic rulers from a higher order, and Judas receives differentiated revelation. It does not establish that Saklas or another local ruler makes the same explicit exclusive-totality boast found in the Yaldabaoth creation-myth family, nor a clean same-agent correction chain.

Gospel_of_Thomas.scope_note: Thomas is a sayings collection with no overarching narrative structure. Hiddenness, interpretation, self-knowledge, and recognition are prominent comparison material, but the lower-ruler and false-local-totality architecture is not established in the checked relevant sayings. This makes Thomas a strong generic-recognition null rather than evidence for the full LAEC graph.

Apocryphon_of_John_control.scope_note: Yaldabaoth is explicitly portrayed as powerful, ignorant of the source of his power, and making an exclusive-divinity claim. The broader narrative contains recognition and repentance, but the clean modern sequence in which that same local ruler receives corrective information and straightforwardly revises his own model is not established as the common textual mechanism.

Hypostasis_and_Origin_Yaldabaoth_family_.scope_note: The Yaldabaoth local-totality boast is strongly supported in this bounded Sethian creation-myth family. Correction and changed allegiance are distributed across roles: Sabaoth explicitly repents and changes relation in relevant witnesses, while Yaldabaoth's own response is not equivalent to the full modern software-style model-revision graph.

Gospel_of_Truth_and_Philip_recognition_c.scope_note: Ignorance, hiddenness, revelation, recognition, awakening, and reorientation are strongly present, but that does not establish a locally powerful ruler falsely claiming that its accessible domain is the totality. These texts reinforce the generic-recognition confounder.
